title: cafaye service manifest
description: Schema for cafaye.yml, the per-service manifest every cafaye repository carries. A manifest is the one place that declares what a thing IS (service or template), its identity, its core spec constraint, the contract surface it exposes and consumes, where each dependency runs per environment, and who owns it. Cross-field rules that JSON Schema cannot express (a published event type must be prefixed by the publishing service; a service never consumes its own events; a consumed type must exist in the core catalog; exposes.api is required for any service that serves traffic; a template declares no events and names a generator instead) are documented in docs/manifest-conventions.md and enforced by tests/test_specs.py.

kind.description: What this entry IS. `service` is a running thing that is resolved, deployed and called. `template` is a thing consumed at GENERATE time: `caf init` renders it and the caller owns the output, so it is versioned and pinned in a registry exactly like a service but is never a running process. Defaults to `service`, so an existing manifest that omits it means what it always meant. A template declares no events and no api, because it has no runtime contract to break.

name.description: The cafaye namespace name. Also the repository name and the value used as the event envelope `source`.

description.description: One sentence on what the service is for. Shown by `caf new` and by pantry.

language.description: Implementation language, or `spec` for specification-only repositories (core itself, contract-test fixtures).

core.description: Constraint on the core spec version this service was written against, e.g. ^0.1.0. Service CI pins core to a release inside this range.

environments.description: Where each dependency runs, per environment. This is the ONLY place self-host-vs-hosted is expressed, and it is a declaration of intent rather than a runtime flag: one manifest says it once, and `caf dev`, `caf deploy` and CI all read the same answer. The `default` environment applies wherever no named environment matches, so a single-environment project needs no block at all. An absent dependency is self-hosted, because the default posture of the platform is that you own what you declare.

exposes.description: The contract surface this service publishes. Omit entirely for libraries, specification-only repositories and templates; a service that serves or receives traffic must declare at least one of api/events.

api.description: Repository-relative path to the OpenAPI 3.1 document describing the HTTP surface.

events.description: Event types this service publishes, as <service>.<entity>.<action>. The first segment must be this manifest's own `name`; see docs/event-naming.md.

consumes.description: Event types this service subscribes to, as <service>.<entity>.<action>. The prefix names the publisher, which is never this service. Delivery is at-least-once, so every consumer must be idempotent.

dependencies.description: Other cafaye services this service builds on. Sync dependencies, not a package manager.

serviceName.description: cafaye namespace rule: lowercase kebab-case, starting with a letter, no trailing separator. 2-40 characters. Reserved: cafaye, caf, kit, core.

provisioning.description: WHERE a dependency runs. `self-hosted` means the caller runs it, in their own compose, on their own machines, with no cafaye account involved. `hosted` means cafaye runs it and the caller consumes it over the network. This is the switch your ethos names — build once, deploy once, use everywhere — and it is declared once, per environment, rather than being discovered at runtime.

environmentResolution.description: Where each of this service's dependencies runs in one environment. Every key is a dependency from `dependencies`; an omitted dependency is self-hosted.

eventType.description: Event type: <service>.<entity>.<action>, exactly three segments. The first segment is a cafaye service name (kebab-case) and must be the publishing service's own `name`; the entity and action segments are lowercase snake_case. See docs/event-naming.md.

semverRange.description: cafaye semver constraint: ^MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, ~MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, >=MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, or an exact MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Prereleases are out of scope for v0.

openapiRef.description: Repository-relative path to an OpenAPI 3.1 document (.yaml, .yml or .json). No leading ./, no absolute paths, no URLs.

version.description: Constraint on the dependency's own contract version.

required.description: false marks a soft dependency: the service runs without it, degraded.

url.description: SSH remote only. HTTPS remotes for cafaye/anywaye repos are a policy violation (PLAN.md §1).

team.description: Owning team in the cafaye namespace.

contact.description: Reachable mailbox for contract and incident questions.
